intro.title: Feature Flag Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable (hook) called `useFeatureFlag` that manages a simple feature flag system. You will learn how to create a reactive state using Vue's `ref` and `computed` to control whether a feature is enabled or disabled. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API and reactive JavaScript. By the end, you will understand how to encapsulate logic in a reusable hook and apply it to conditionally render UI components based on the flag's value.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are used in real-world applications to control feature visibility without redeploying code. For example, e-commerce platforms use them to gradually roll out new checkout flows, while SaaS dashboards toggle experimental analytics panels for specific user segments. Developers implement feature flag hooks to conditionally render UI components like modals, forms, or entire sections, enabling A/B testing and controlled releases. This pattern allows teams to manage features dynamically, reducing risk and improving user experience.
